title: DeepMind reveals Gemini Robotics 2.5 and open safety benchmark "ASIMOV-jailbreak"
gist: Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2.5 VLA model posts 30-100% higher success and 20-30% faster execution than its predecessor and hit 96% success kitting parts in Mercedes-Benz factories on Apptronik Apollo 2 humanoids, but still runs in the cloud with latency and faces a 'steep road' to close the last 4%. DeepMind also open-sourced ASIMOV-Jailbreak, a 1,500-prompt physical-AI safety benchmark.

insights.claim: Google DeepMind's physical AI stack splits into Gemini Embodied Reasoning (a vision-language model that plans tasks from live video) and Gemini Robotics (a vision-language-action model that generates actuator commands), with the VLA layer now at version 2.5.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: The planner/actuator split is the emerging reference architecture for humanoid AI; watch which layers partners license versus build.
insights.locator: DeepMind's physical AI platform has several computational layers

insights.claim: Gemini Robotics 2.5 achieves a 30 to 100 percent higher task success rate and runs 20 to 30 percent faster than the previous version in laboratory testing across more than 200 activities.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Rapid generation-over-generation gains suggest general-purpose robot foundation models are on a steep improvement curve.
insights.locator: Overall, Gemini Robotics 2.5 manages a 30 to 100 percent

insights.claim: Apptronik's Apollo 2 humanoid running Gemini Robotics 2.5 can tie a bow with five-fingered hands, a milestone because deformable objects like ribbon are notoriously hard for robots to manipulate.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Deformable-object dexterity unlocks textiles, packaging and lab-handling use cases previously out of reach for automation.
insights.locator: Google also showed that Apptronik's Apollo 2

insights.claim: Gemini-powered Apptronik Apollo 2 humanoids kitted automotive parts in several European Mercedes-Benz factories at a 96 percent success rate.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: First credible real-factory humanoid metric from a frontier lab; benchmark for competing humanoid programs pitching automakers.
insights.locator: Google partnered with Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz

insights.claim: A 96 percent success rate is likely still insufficient for automakers like Mercedes-Benz because humans doing repetitive kitting tasks are right virtually every time, and DeepMind expects closing the remaining 4 percent gap to be hard.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Commercial humanoid revenue timelines hinge on the reliability tail, not headline capability — temper near-term deployment expectations.
insights.quote: closing that last 4 percent gap will be a “steep road.”
insights.locator: That's an impressive showing compared to previous robotic AI systems

insights.claim: General-purpose robot AI faces an explicit trade-off between per-application reliability and generalization; DeepMind is choosing to push generalization even if it means not reaching 99.9 percent on every task.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Specialized automation vendors retain an edge on narrow high-reliability tasks while generalist humanoids target breadth — a key segmentation for robotics investing.
insights.quote: Or we can just push on the generalization axis and maybe not get to 99.9 in every application.
insights.locator: “We can be very good at a particular application

insights.claim: Scarcity of physical-world training data is the core bottleneck for robot AI; DeepMind used its Gemini 4 Argon model as a simulation engine to generate thousands of digital-twin variations from real camera data, blended with teleoperation demonstrations.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Frontier LLMs becoming synthetic-data engines for robotics favors labs that own both a top general model and a robotics stack.

insights.claim: Gemini Robotics 2.5 still runs on cloud-based servers rather than embedded hardware, so its accuracy and speed gains come with latency, and DeepMind's demo video was sped up 2x.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: On-device inference for robots remains unsolved — an opening for edge AI silicon and a caveat on demo videos.
insights.quote: The video above is sped up by 2x to make the robot look more human-like.
insights.locator: Argon was also used for analyzing failures

insights.claim: Gemini Robotics 2.5's inference-time hazard reasoning let robots safely complete tasks 33 percent more often with obstacles present and 43 percent more often when people were in the way.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Human-proximity safety is a gating factor for co-working humanoids and for insurer/regulator acceptance.
insights.locator: DeepMind is also working to ensure the failures

insights.claim: DeepMind released ASIMOV-Jailbreak, an open-source dataset of 1,500 prompts designed to trick robotic AI into unsafe actions, on Hugging Face, aiming to set an industry standard where none exists for testing physical AI safety.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Whoever defines the de facto embodied-AI safety benchmark shapes future regulation and procurement criteria.
insights.locator: There is no agreed-upon way to test physical AI for safety

insights.claim: Adding Gemini 4 Argon into the loop lifts DeepMind's robot jailbreak safety score to 98.8 percent, versus 73.5 percent with Gemini Robotics ER 2 alone.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Safety depends on pairing robots with large frontier models, reinforcing cloud dependence and compute demand for robotics.
insights.locator: DeepMind says that placing Argon in the loop

insights.claim: Gemini Robotics 2.5 is not generally available but has been delivered to Google's robotics partners Agile Robots, Apptronik and Boston Dynamics.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Google is positioning as the 'Android of robots' model supplier to hardware makers rather than building its own humanoid.
insights.locator: Gemini Robotics 2.5 is not generally available
